articles.title: Steelers Icon Jerome Bettis Sounds Off on Aaron Rodgers, Mike McCarthy in Video, 'Disappointed'
articles.summary: During Friday's pregame show on Prime Video, Pittsburgh Steelers legend Jerome Bettis said he "disappointed" by the entire situation surrounding his former team and quarterback Aaron Rodgers.
articles.body:
During Friday's pregame show on Prime Video, Pittsburgh Steelers legend Jerome Bettis said he "disappointed" by the entire situation surrounding his former team and quarterback Aaron Rodgers.

Bettis said Rodgers "didn't pick the right time" to air out his grievances, but questioned how the team would handle the adversity moving forward.

"You can't unhear what [Rodgers] said," Bettis said. "So now, the question is, the culture of that Pittsburgh Steeler locker room, how do they respond from all of this? ... How do you recover from something like this?"

The 42-year-old quarterback made an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday, a day after the team announced he would be benched, and accused Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy of sleeping through meetings, among other things. Rodgers was released the same day.

The Steelers entered Friday's game against the Denver Broncos with a 6-4 record, placing them second in the AFC North behind only the Cincinnati Bengals. Pittsburgh will lean on backup quarterback Mason Rudolph as its starter for the foreseeable future. He started one game last season, which resulted in a 31-28 loss against the Chicago Bears.

articles.title: Broncos' Alex Singleton Uses Aaron Rodgers' Iconic Celebration in Trending Video Amid Steelers Drama
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers may no longer be a member of the Pittsburgh Steelers, but there was little chance he wouldn't be referenced on the field in some way during the Black Friday game against the Denver Broncos.
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers may no longer be a member of the Pittsburgh Steelers, but there was little chance he wouldn't be referenced on the field in some way during the Black Friday game against the Denver Broncos.

Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton found the right moment to invoke the outspoken quarterback by using his signature "Discount Double Check" celebration after tackling Steelers running back Jaylen Warren in the end zone for a safety.

Friday marks the first time the Steelers are playing since all of the drama with Rodgers unfolded, starting with the announcement he would be inactive against the Broncos.

Things escalated quickly from there when Rodgers went on The Pat McAfee Show to unload on Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy, leading to him being released by the club.

Rodgers adopted the "Discount Double Check" celebration in the early-2010s after landing an endorsement deal with State Farm. He didn't use as much later in his career, though it did make an appearance late last season against the Baltimore Ravens when he scored a rushing touchdown.

articles.title: Liberal media and fans want Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker to fail because he's a Catholic conservative
articles.summary: Harrison Butker's critics, including Mina Kimes and Nick Wright, claim his activism has hurt his play, but his stats tell a more complicated story.
articles.body: Few NFL players have drawn as much personal disdain from the political left as Kansas City Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker. The outspoken Catholic conservative has become a target for liberal sports fans and media personalities since delivering his 2024 commencement address at Benedictine College. His public support for Donald Trump, the Republican Party, campaigning with Senator Josh Hawley, and advocacy for traditional family values have only intensified that criticism. Butker has been branded a misogynist for expressing the belief that motherhood is more fulfilling for women than climbing the corporate ladder. A stance that clearly aligns with his Catholic faith and those that attend Benedictine College, a Catholic college, which he was speaking too directly. Since then, as we have seen from some of his most vocal critics, watching Butker miss field goals over the years, especially this season, appears to provide a sense of political vindication. Unfortunately, the three-time Super Bowl champion has given those critics plenty of ammunition this season from media and fans. WIFE OF PATRICK MAHOMES UNLEASHES FIRE AND FURY TOWARDS REFS AFTER BOTCHED CALL IN BUFFALO Mina Kimes, Nick Wright, and Other Media and Fans Have Butker Living Rent Free Many media members are still taking shots at Butker for his comments in the commencement speech years later. On Pablo Torre's Thanksgiving episode, he invited ESPN's Mina Kimes and the clip shared on X had a caption that said, "Harrison Butker may not like our Thanksgiving episode." The clip featured a male cook preparing some Thanksgiving dishes. Mina Kimes, still clearly triggered by Butker said, "How triggered do you think Harrison Butker would be if he turned this on and saw a bunch of men cooking for me?" Good grief. MINA KIMES CRACKS HARRISON BUTKER JOKE ABOUT MEN IN THE KITCHEN WITH CALLBACK TO KICKER'S COMMENCEMENT SPEECH After the Chiefs worst game of the season on Sunday Night Football against the Seattle Seahawks, also being Butker's worst game of the season, going 1-for-3 on field goals, Nick Wright took a political shot at Butker. "He started splitting his time between football and activism, and he hasn't been quite as good. That is just the timeline of it," Wright said. There's clearly a political bias here and even making this topic political is unprofessional, in my opinion. Also, Butker didn't immediately regress after becoming more politically outspoken. In fact, he converted every field goal and extra point he attempted between campaigning with Senator Josh Hawley during the Chiefs bye week in 2024 and suffering his knee injury. Maybe Wright should've spoken about how the knee injury and becoming the NFL's highest paid kicker could have effected Butker's performance. On Thanksgiving fans took plenty of shots at Butker after missing a crucial 46-yard field goal with the game tied against the Buffalo Bills. Denver news anchor Kyle Clark posted on X, "Butker. Wide right. Happy Thanksgiving, America." He later responded to a comment about rooting for and against players based on political party affiliation, Clark said, "Hi anonymous friend. Happy to clear this up for you. Whether my wife and my daughters should be able to have a job is not politics. It’s human rights. Have a Happy Thanksgiving!" Again, a false retelling of what Butker said and believes. Former Minnesota Star Tribune journalist Jim Souhan said, "Someone said that Butker’s pronouns are Miss/Misses and I’ll never forget it." Editor-in Chief at radically liberal news outlet Meidas Touch, Ron Filipkowski took a shot as well by sharing a photo of Butker with President Trump on top of a post from an Associated Press reporter that stated, "Harrison Butker is tied with Trey Smack for most missed kicks this season with 9 (8 FGs, 1 PAT) and his 24 missed kicks (17 FGs, 7 PATs) since start of 2024 are most in NFL." Obviously, when Butker misses to the right, the jokes write themselves, so those don't bother me. It's the low-hanging fruit that is easy to pick. What we do need to discuss is how bad Butker has been statistically can be somewhat misleading. Butker's Struggles Are Real, But The Numbers Need Context In August 2024, 86 days after his controversial commencement speech at Benedictine College, the Kansas City Chiefs rewarded Butker with a four-year, $25.6 million contract extension, making him the highest-paid kicker in NFL history at the time. Whether you're right, left, or center, you could agree at that time, Butker deserved this. The Chiefs clearly did not care that liberals were calling for Butker to be cut from the team for his comments on traditional roles within the household. Butker was coming off a 2023 campaign in which he converted 33 of his 35 field goal attempts and made every extra point. He also drilled a Super Bowl-record 57-yard field goal against the San Francisco 49ers. He was arguably the Super Bowl MVP for much of the game. Unfortunately, his field goal percentage has declined every season since signing that lucrative extension. Butker currently owns the worst field goal percentage among NFL kickers with at least 15 attempts this season. However, a closer examination of his numbers reveals that his struggles are overwhelmingly concentrated in one area: long-distance field goals. According to NFL.com, Butker has converted just two of his eight attempts from 50-plus yards this season (25%). From inside 50 yards, he's 13-of-15 (86.7%), including a perfect 7-of-7 from inside 40 yards. It's particulary shocking to see how bad he's been from distance because he hit a 69-yard field goal in preseason, which most likely would've been good from almost 80 yards. HARRISON BUTKER'S 69-YARD FIELD GOAL DEMONSTRATES THE NFL'S LATEST BIG SCORING CONTROVERSY Butker isn't the only highly compensated kicker struggling from deep, either. Dallas Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey, who surpassed Butker as the highest-paid kicker in NFL history after signing a four-year, $28 million extension in April, is also experiencing the worst season of his career. Aubrey has converted just six of his 11 attempts from 50-plus yards (54.5%) and is shooting a career-low 77.8% overall. He also missed a 40-yard field goal on Thanksgiving in Dallas' one-point loss to Philadelphia. That kick has been heavily debated online, with former Colts punter and placeholder Pat McAfee giving Aubrey grace because the laces were facing toward Aubrey. Speaking about Aubrey's stats are not an excuse for Butker's poor performance, but it does provide some much-needed perspective. Clearly his struggles are not as scrutinized as Butker's, though he's paid more. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The Best Revenge Is Success There is a difference between rooting for someone to fail because of their religious and political beliefs and legitimately criticizing their professional performance. Butker deserves the latter right now. If you know me at all, I am not a LeBron James fan. Yes, his politics come into play in my dislike of him, but claiming poor play is because of campaigning for Hilary Clinton or Kamala Harris by me would hopefully cause many to scold me for refusing to provide proper sports analysis and instead, going for a political cheapshot. In all honestly, I'd love nothing more than to see Butker return to being one of the most reliable kickers in football. But defending his right to express his Catholic faith and conservative values doesn't require defending his inability to consistently put a football through the uprights, especially from long distance. The Chiefs are paying him elite money to deliver elite results, particularly in high-pressure situations with championship aspirations on the line. He has no one to blame but himself. He needs to be better. Butker doesn't need to apologize for his faith, his political affiliations or his appreciation for traditional family values. He just needs to start making kicks again. Until he does that, his critics, in and out of the media, will continue to tee off on who they consider to be their political enemy.

Brock Purdy has been ruled out for the San Francisco 49ers' NFC West clash with the Seattle Seahawks.

Purdy did not practice on Wednesday and Thursday. He wasn't seen at the start of 49ers practice on Friday either, and the team made the decision on Friday that Mac Jones would start in Week 12.

Brock Purdy's ankle kept him out of practice once again on Friday.

The San Francisco 49ers quarterback missed practice on Wednesday and Thursday because of the ankle ailment.

Regardless of if he plays or not, Purdy faces a tough matchup versus the Seattle defense. Seattle leads the NFL with 236.1 total yards allowed per game. Minnesota is second with 280.3 yards conceded per contest.

Seattle's allowed less than 14 points in three of its last four games. The Seahawks gave up 20 points in two meetings with the 49ers last year.

The waiver-wire options to replace Purdy are limited because of the five games that have already been played in Week 12.

Josh Johnson is a long-shot pickup because he faces a Washington defense that gives up the second-most passing yards in the NFL.

Derrick Henry Participates in Full At Friday Practice

Henry is going up against a Houston defense that gives up the eighth-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL.

Henry struggled against the Texans last season with 33 yards on 15 carries. He did score a touchdown in that matchup.

The Baltimore running back is typically a must-start player in fantasy football matchups, but it's understandable to have some hesitation with the matchup against Houston.

articles.title: Chargers QB Justin Herbert (concussion) to miss Week 12, DJ Uiagalelei will make first NFL start vs. Patriots
articles.summary: DJ Uiagalelei will make his first NFL start in Herbert's place.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers have ruled out quarterback Justin Herbert (concussion) for their Week 12 matchup against the New England Patriots, the team announced Friday .

Herbert was placed in concussion protocol following last week's 27-24 loss to the New York Jets. He did not practice this week before the team confirmed that the 28-year-old will not play.

DJ Uiagalelei will make his first NFL start in Herbert's place. Jake Browning, who was signed to the Chargers' active roster this week, will serve as the backup.

"This isn't my first rodeo with regard to starting quarterbacks having an injury you don't know at the beginning of the week when we start game planning," said Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, who experienced similar concussion issues at the quarterback position when he coached the Miami Dolphins and Tua Tagovailoa.

Uiagalelei is a former elite high school prospect who took a circuitous route to his first NFL start. One of the top quarterback recruits in his class, he appeared destined to follow in Trevor Lawrence's footsteps at Clemson, but struggled to replicate that success once given the starting job. He wound up spending the last two years of his college career at Oregon State and Florida State.

He went unselected in the 2025 NFL Draft and has spent most of his professional career on the Chargers' practice squad, but moved to the backup role in October after an injury to Trey Lance. Now, he will be under center against the defending AFC champions.

The 1-9 Chargers are tied for the worst record in the NFL entering Week 12. Following Sunday's game against the Patriots, Jim Harbaugh's team goes on the road back-to-back weeks to take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Las Vegas Raiders before welcoming the San Francisco 49ers at home in Week 15.

articles.title: Justin Herbert Injury Update, D.J. Uiagalelei Set to Make 1st NFL Start for Chargers vs. Patriots
articles.summary: Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert will not be available on Sunday against the New England Patriots due to a concussion.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert will not be available on Sunday against the New England Patriots due to a concussion.

The Chargers announced on Friday that Herbert will sit out, putting D.J. Uiagalelei in line to make his first career NFL start.

Herbert was placed in concussion protocol on Monday after playing all 60 offensive snaps in the Chargers' 27-24 loss to the New York Jets.

Uiagalelei has spent his entire NFL career with the Chargers after signing with the team as an undrafted free agent in 2025. He made his first appearance in a game in Week 9, taking 15 snaps in the fourth quarter of a 44-22 loss to the Houston Texans.

The 25-year-old Uiagalelei played five college seasons with three different programs from 2020 to '24. He started 45 games during that period, including leading Clemson to the ACC Championship in 2022.

The injury adds another chapter to what's been a frustrating year for Herbert.

The 28-year-old has thrown for 1,851 yards, eight touchdowns and 11 interceptions in 2026 as the Chargers have started the season 1-9.

Herbert had a strong 2025 campaign with 3,727 yards, 26 touchdowns and 13 interceptions, but has failed to get things going under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel.

Third-string quarterback Trey Lance is currently on the injured reserve with a groin injury, so the Chargers signed Jake Browning earlier this week to add more depth to their quarterback room.

The Chargers host the Patriots at SoFi Stadium on Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers Was 'Barred' from Steelers' Facility Before Mike McCarthy Remarks, QB Reveals Details
articles.summary: In the time after he was benched in favor of Mason Rudolph and before he got released, Aaron Rodgers was not allowed at the Pittsburgh Steelers' facilities on Wednesday.
articles.body:
In the time after he was benched in favor of Mason Rudolph and before he got released, Aaron Rodgers was not allowed at the Pittsburgh Steelers' facilities on Wednesday.

Prime Video play-by-play broadcaster Al Michaels said during Friday's telecast of the Steelers-Broncos game that Rodgers texted him to say he was "barred" from the team's facility prior to his release.

After the Steelers announced late Tuesday night that Rodgers would be inactive for the Broncos game, it was noted the next morning that he wasn't present for the start of their practice.

Per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero , Rodgers was "excused" from coming to the facilities.

As Michaels read in the text he received from Rodgers, he "never heard" from Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy about the benching and it was after he was "barred" from the facility that he decided to go on The Pat McAfee Show .

The appearance with Pat McAfee saw Rodgers seemingly air out every grievance he had with McCarthy dating back to their time together with the Green Bay Packers.

After Rodgers' appearance on the show, the Steelers announced they released the four-time NFL MVP.

Among the key takeaways from Rodgers was McCarthy fell asleep multiple times in team meetings recently, said "1-2-3, Packers" to break down the team huddle coming out of the locker room for the second half in Sunday's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles and questioned how healthy he was.

"It began as a concerned friend. … If you're falling asleep in meetings, you're unhealthy," Rodgers said.

ESPN's Brooke Pryor corroborated some of Rodgers' story. McCarthy himself admitted to the "1-2-3, Packers" blunder, calling it an "embarrassing" but honest mistake.

Rodgers went unclaimed on waivers , making him a free agent eligible to sign with any team for the remainder of the season. There's no indication of interest from a club, nor that he wants to sign at this point.

The 42-year-old Rodgers said back in the spring after signing with the Steelers this would be his final season. He finished his tenure in Pittsburgh with 2,241 passing yards and 16 touchdowns in 10 starts this season.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers Trolled by NFL Fans After Mike McCarthy, Steelers Upset Nix, Broncos After QB's Exit
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers began life after Aaron Rodgers with a resounding 27-5 win over the visiting Denver Broncos on Friday afternoon.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers began life after Aaron Rodgers with a resounding 27-5 win over the visiting Denver Broncos on Friday afternoon.

The Steelers' defense ruled the day with two touchdowns. Edge-rusher TJ Watt recovered a fumble in the end zone after a team sack of Broncos quarterback Bo Nix for the first one, and cornerback Jalen Ramsey got a pick-six on Nix for the second score.

The Mason Rudolph-led offense wasn't flashy, but it certainly got the job done. Rudolph completed 9.5 yards per attempt (9-of-15, 142 yards) and found wide receiver DK Metcalf for a 22-yard score.

Steelers running backs Rico Dowdle and Jaylen Warren also combined for 117 yards.

The Rodgers era ended quickly earlier this week. On Tuesday evening, the Steelers made Rodgers inactive and announced Rudolph as the starter.

On Wednesday afternoon, Rodgers went on the Pat McAfee Show and went off on his former head coach, Mike McCarthy, levying a host of different criticisms.

Shortly after the interview, the Steelers announced they released Rodgers.

Steelers owner Art Rooney II spoke with Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette about the matter that "insubordination will not be tolerated" and gave a full vote of confidence to McCarthy.

"I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he'll be our coach this season, next season and beyond. The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can't be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can't live with that."

McCarthy's Steelers certainly got the post-Rodgers era off to a great start over an 8-2 Broncos team that was in second place alone in the AFC standings before the game began. Denver averaged 30.5 points per game over its last four weeks but could only manage a field goal on offense against the ferocious Steeler D.

Fans and analysts noted how well the Steelers performed post-Rodgers on Friday.

Pittsburgh will now enjoy a long weekend and return to the field on Sunday, Dec. 6, when it hosts the Houston Texans for a Sunday Night Football matchup.

articles.title: NFL: Pittsburgh Steelers shock Denver Broncos 27-5 after Aaron Rodgers drama dominates build-up following Mike McCarthy claims
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers stun the Denver Broncos 27-5 in their first game since releasing four-time MVP quarterback Aaron Rodgers following his remarkable comments regarding head coach Mike McCarthy; Rodgers had accused McCarthy of falling asleep in meetings
articles.body:
Broncos quarterback Bo Nix endured a miserable afternoon as he surrendered two interceptions and a lost fumble that resulted in two defensive touchdowns for the Steelers.

Denver trailed 24-5 after a dire first half in which they were limited to just 58 yards of offense, becoming just the third team since 1991 to post fewer than 60 yards while conceding two defensive touchdowns over the first two quarters of a game.

TJ Watt scored with an end zone fumble recovery, Jalen Ramsey returned a Nix interception to the house and D.K. Metcalf recorded a touchdown catch before appearing to celebrate by holding up eight fingers in an apparent support of Rodgers.

The Broncos looked anything but a contender as they slumped to 8-3, while the Steelers distanced themselves from a reflection of turmoil to improve to 7-4 in their push for the playoffs.

The Rodgers saga had lingered as an unwelcome backdrop heading into the game after the four-time MVP quarterback was released this week in the wake of his sensational appearance on the Pat McAfee Show.

Rodgers had claimed that head coach McCarthy fell asleep in team meetings, rebuffed suggestions to connect better with Pittsburgh's defensive players and accidentally shouted "one, two, three, Packers!" at the end of a team talk against the Philadelphia Eagles, the latter of which McCarthy would admit as an embarrassing moment.

Rodgers was subsequently cut amid what is set to mark the final season of his NFL career, though the storyline resurfaced during the game as broadcaster Al Michaels read a supposed text from the 42-year-old in which he is said to have claimed the Steelers had "barred" him from the team facility after he was benched for Mason Rudolph.

Rudolph started in place of Rodgers for the first time since the incident as he went nine of 15 passing for 142 yards and a touchdown, while Rico Dowdle and Jaylen Warren combined for 117 yards on the ground.

Reflecting on their win after such an eventful week, Rudolph said: "We just sort of rallied around Coach McCarthy, and I think in a weird way, the adversity brought us brought us closer together.

"It was a lot. Sort of unprecedented - certainly like nothing I've ever been through, and probably the same for all of my team-mates.

"I'm just so proud of the way we turned the page from [Aaron Rodgers' release on] Wednesday, and the veteran leadership - the Cam Haywards, the Jalen Ramseys, the TJ Watts - they really led us forward."

It took until 9.23 remaining in the third quarter for the first first down of the second half to arrive when the struggling Nix connected with Jaylen Waddle for 22 yards.

Still, it would come up empty amid a sequence of five successive punts between the teams, until Denver turned the ball over when Zach Allen forced a fumble from Dowdle that was recovered by Riley Moss with 3.31 on the clock.

Such was the story of their night that Denver failed to capitalise as their resulting drive ended in Wil Lutz missing a 53-yard field goal at the beginning of the fourth quarter.

Rudolph followed up by launching a downfield strike to Roman Wilson for 37 yards to set up Chris Boswell's 33-yard field goal for a 27-5 lead with 11.16 to play.

Nix's turnover issues resumed when he was intercepted by Daylen Everette at Pittsburgh's seven-yard line to ultimately end the game.

Passing: Bo Nix, 22/40, 169 yards, 2 INTs

Rushing: Cody Schrader, 7 carries, 27 yards

Receiving: Jaylen Waddle, 5 catches, 53 yards

Passing: Mason Rudolph, 9/15, 142 yards, 1 TD

Rushing: Rico Dowdle, 11 carries, 71 yards

Receiving: Germie Bernard, 1 catch, 58 yards

For so long defense has been the heartbeat of the Steelers operation, and it leapt to the occasion in the opening exchanges by way of TJ Watt as their stalwart edge rusher downed Nix's finger-slip fumble in the end zone for a deadlock-breaking touchdown in the first quarter.

Pittsburgh then forced a swift three-and-out to pave the way for Rudolph's 22-yard touchdown strike to Metcalf, who did outstandingly to haul in a back-pedalling catch while facing man coverage from star corner Pat Surtain II.

Denver turned to their own defense as a potential route back into the game when Alex Singleton stuffed Warren in the end zone for a safety, before Lutz and Boswell exchanged a pair of 44 and 47-yard field goals.

The Steelers then stretched their lead with a second defensive first-half touchdown when Ramsey turned a Nix interception into a 36-yard slaloming pick-six with 1.33 to play.

A strange week for the Pittsburgh Steelers that included former quarterback Aaron Rodgers' benching, his airing of dirty laundry regarding head coach Mike McCarthy on the Pat McAfee Show , Pittsburgh's release of Rodgers and the Steelers publicly going to bat for their coach culminated with a dominant 27-5 home win over the AFC West-leading Denver Broncos on Friday afternoon.

Watts, really led us forward and so thankful to God for keeping me here eight years later, would never have thought, thank you to [owner Art Rooney II] for paying my bills."

Watt and cornerback Jalen Ramsey coupled with holding Denver's offense to just one field goal, Pittsburgh did enough on offense to get it done. articles.title: Aaron Rodgers releases new statement via Al Michaels, says he went on 'Pat McAfee Show' after Steelers barred him from team facility

Prime Video broadcaster Al Michaels relayed a text message he got from the former MVP during the game which attempted to rebut some of his critics and explain why he handled things the way he did. Michaels read the text messages early in the fourth quarter of the Black Friday game.

That rebuttal could be aimed at a number of notable figures:

Rodgers' quarterbacking peer Tom Brady said, " The sanctity of an NFL locker room, it's a very sacred place. "

One day later, Rodgers appeared on the Pat McAfee Show and trashed head coach Mike McCarthy, alleging that McCarthy showed up late to meetings and fell asleep during them:

Hours later, the Steelers released Rodgers, perhaps bringing his Hall of Fame career to an end.

articles.title: Tee Higgins Injury Update, Latest on Bengals WR's Hamstring and Status for Saints Game
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints, according to the team's injury report.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints, according to the team's injury report .

The 27-year-old missed practice on Friday due to a hamstring injury, but head coach Zac Taylor offered reassurances about his availability after the team's practice.

"Yeah," Taylor said when asked if Higgins will play Sunday, per ESPN's Ben Baby . "He just woke up sore today. We just gave him the day [off] and we'll see where he's at."

Higgins has been an integral part of Cincinnati's No. 3 scoring offense this season. He has recorded 55 catches for 867 yards with seven touchdowns in 10 games. He's averaged a career-high 86.7 yards per game and a team-high 15.8 yards per reception.

"There are certain guys where if I ever feel like we need to be careful with them in practice, I'm going to lean that way, just because I've seen them," Taylor said, per Baby. "I've seen the reps. They've repped the plays we're going to run a million times. I'm not concerned about it."

Higgins has missed time with hamstring injuries in the past, and the Bengals could find it difficult to replace his production if he were to miss time. Outside of Cincinnati's two star wide receivers, no other Bengals player has reached 400 receiving yards this season. The Bengals have also struggled to move the ball on the ground — their 794 rushing yards are the third-fewest by any team this season.

Cincinnati is hoping to get back in the win column after suffering a 22-20 loss against the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football. Although the Bengals still sit atop the AFC North, that loss didn't leave much room for error. The Pittsburgh Steelers improved to 7-4 with a win over the Denver Broncos, and another loss would leave Cincinnati's fate up to tiebreakers for the division title.

articles.title: While Aaron Rodgers defends himself by texting Al Michaels, the Steelers press on without him
articles.summary: PITTSBURGH (AP) — The love and respect inside the Pittsburgh Steelers' locker room for Aaron Rodgers is real. And it seems neither — in the short term anyway...
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH (AP) — The love and respect inside the Pittsburgh Steelers' locker room for Aaron Rodgers is real.

It also isn't going anywhere. And it seems neither — in the short term anyway — is Rodgers.

The four-time NFL MVP, watching Pittsburgh's 27-5 victory over Denver on Friday from afar after his stunning dismissal earlier in the week, felt compelled to try and reclaim the narrative on national television for the second time in three days, even as his former team tried to turn the page.

Rodgers texted play-by-play announcer Al Michaels during the Amazon Prime broadcast, defending his decision to go on ESPN's "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday and eviscerate Steelers coach Mike McCarthy .

Some — including former Pittsburgh coach turned TV commentator Mike Tomlin — took exception to Rodgers bringing issues normally kept behind closed doors into the light. Rodgers, as he has consistently done throughout a 22-year career that appears to be over, didn't back down.

"A lot of talk about the sanctity of the locker room," Rodgers said in the text, according to Michaels. "The code or sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership."

During his ESPN appearance, Rodgers raised concerns about McCarthy's mental and physical well-being, saying that McCarthy would fall asleep during meetings and invoked the name of the Green Bay Packers instead of the Steelers while addressing the team at halftime of a loss to Philadelphia last week. McCarthy confirmed that he mistakenly said "1-2-3 Packers," calling the reference to one of his former teams an "embarrassing moment."

The team benched Rodgers late Tuesday night, then cut him not long after his blistering remarks.

"They took this public," Rodgers wrote in the text, according to Michaels. "Never heard from the head coach. Then they leaked at 11 p.m. They also barred me from the facility. That's why I went to McAfee."

That part may be a stretch. For the Steelers to ban Rodgers from the facility, he would have be suspended first, or else the team would be violating the NFL's collective bargaining agreement. Since he wasn't officially disciplined after issuing an ultimatum to McCarthy earlier in the week over play-calling, the Steelers instead excused Rodgers from practice on Wednesday, knowing his relationship with the team was going to be severed.

His relationship with McCarthy and the front office anyway.

The bond Rodgers created with his now-former teammates runs deeper .

"I love Aaron to death," linebacker Patrick Queen said. "Probably one of the coolest teammates I ever had, just the conversations that we had. My stance isn't going to change. I don't think anybody's stance (will) change on that."

Which can make things tricky. After Rodgers' dismissal, McCarthy brought the team's leadership council — a group that includes defensive tackle Cam Heyward, linebacker T.J. Watt and now-starting quarterback Mason Rudolph — together to address a variety of topics.

Who knows if that would have happened if Rodgers had not spoken up. While both Watt and Heyward said after the game that only time will tell if the team will find itself on better footing with McCarthy — who has the support of team president Art Rooney II — the loss of Rodgers will linger.

"Very hard, very challenging," Rudolph said. "I mean, on one hand, you're thankful for the time you spent with him and everything you learned football-wise and the friendship. But we obviously had a lot of stuff we had to filter through."

They weren't the only ones. The 66,000-plus fans who spent three hours in a nonstop chilly rain began the afternoon on edge. They erupted with joy when Watt recovered Broncos quarterback Bo Nix's fumble in the end zone for a first-quarter touchdown. The roar was even louder during Jalen Ramsey's pick-6 late in the first half.

By the time rookie cornerback Daylan Everette intercepted Nix in the fourth quarter to end the competitive portion of the game, a small group of fans could be heard repeating a profane and hardly friendly chant about Rodgers.

Those feelings are not shared by the men wearing black and gold who began the season wanting to help give Rodgers an appropriate send-off for a career that will almost certainly lead to him donning a gold jacket at the Pro Football Hall of Fame in a few years.

That send-off will never come. Yet the Steelers — who at 7-4 have a strong chance of making the playoffs — know they still must press forward.

"Hopefully we grow from it," Heyward said. "That's all I can hope for."

articles.title: Chiefs Finally Stopped Josh Allen, With Help From Buffalo Weather
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs have struggled with the Buffalo quarterback, but the awful weather helped stop him.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs have long lamented their inability to stop quarterback Josh Allen of the Buffalo Bills, but they finally managed to do it with a huge assist from the Buffalo weather. Allen threw for just 81 yards in the Chiefs' 13-10 loss, and ultimately this will go down as a lost opportunity.

Allen is usually unaffected by bad weather, as he's as used to playing in snow and other ghastly weather as any quarterback in the league. But he looked completely flummoxed by the awful conditions, which featured a driving rain and an unpredictable swirling wind.

The Buffalo quarterback finished with a stat line of 10-for-21 for 81 yards and a pair of interceptions, and his longest completion of the game went for just 17 yards to Khalil Shakir. He did generate 43 yards on the ground on seven carries, but it was one of the Chiefs' best defensive performances ever against the Buffalo star.

Allen looked out of sorts on many of this throws, as he couldn't control how the ball was coming out of his hands on several. He was outplayed by quarterback Patrick Mahomes, although Mahomes' line wasn't outstanding either as he completed 16-of-29 for 174 yards.

The player the Chiefs couldn't control was running back James Cook III. Cook was a workhorse in this one, which was largely dictated by the conditions, as he rushed for 117 yards on 32 carries, including the Bills' only touchdown of the game.

It was Cook who provided the plays Allen couldn't. Many of his runs were stuffed at the line of scrimmage, and Cook's longest run of the day was for 10 yards, with Allen adding a 17-yard effort on one of his runs. But he came through with tough yards when they mattered, and he was the offensive star of this contest.

The loss put the Chiefs two games behind the Bills, and many are writing the Chiefs off as a possible No. 1 seed in the AFC.

Don't buy it, though. Buffalo may be 10-1 right now, but every team goes through a rough stretch sooner or later, and the Bill still have games against the Green Bay Packers, Chicago Bears and Denver Broncos coming up.

This win does clinch a vital tiebreaker for Buffalo, and that may matter in January. But there's still a lot of season left to play, and it's far too early to carve anything in stone right now. The Chiefs could still meet Allen and company down the road, and it would be fun to see this matchup again under better conditions.

articles.title: Broncos’ Nik Bonitto gets 100% real on getting ‘whooped’ by Steelers
articles.summary: As the Denver Broncos delivered a disappointing 27-5 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Friday, there’s no denying that the team got humbled after winning th...
articles.body:
As the Denver Broncos delivered a disappointing 27-5 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Friday, there's no denying that the team got humbled after winning the last six games. With the Broncos' loss led by a down outing from quarterback Bo Nix , linebacker Nik Bonitto would speak candidly about Denver's performance as a whole.

Speaking after the defeat in his post-game press conference in the locker room, Bonitto kept it real about how Pittsburgh beat the Broncos on Friday.

"They just came out and whooped us," Bonitto said, according to Zac Stevens.

There's no doubt that all eyes will be on Denver's offense, as they only scored three points the entire game, with the other two coming on a safety in the second quarter. Looking at Nix, he threw for 169 yards and two interceptions, but head coach Sean Payton would take full accountability for the loss.

"Well, obviously, disappointing loss…it starts with me," Payton said, via Stevens. "You know, I felt like our prep coming into this week, relative to the schedule, was good. You know, we knew it was going to be a tough challenge coming in here; they played well at home, and I think early on, we gave them opportunities of momentum, and that falls on me."

The Broncos struggled in all areas, with Nix giving the Steelers many opportunities to flourish, such as a fumble that led to a touchdown for T.J. Watt and a pick-six by Jalen Ramsey towards the end of the first half. At any rate, Denver looks to improve with Dec. 6's matchup against the Miami Dolphins.

articles.title: Analyst thinks T.J. Hockenson can be a top receiving option
articles.summary: T.J. Hockenson could find an increased role in the Vikings' offense down the stretch.
articles.body:
Minnesota Vikings TE T.J. Hockenson has been perhaps the offense's most consistent weapon through 10 games in 2026. He ranks second on the team in receptions (41), receiving yards (383), and touchdown receptions (three). Hockenson appeared to have the best rapport with Kyler Murray before the quarterback was sidelined with a hamstring injury in Week 9.

Although Hockenson was inactive for Kirk Cousins' first game back with the Vikings in Week 10, the tight end returned in Week 11 and showed he can provide the offense with a valuable change of pace. He caught six passes for 55 yards, picking up four first downs against the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday night.

Bleacher Report 's Brent Sobleski believes Hockenson can continue to provide balance to an offense built around Justin Jefferson.

"Minnesota's offense can become predictable because everyone knows Jefferson will get his targets," Sobleski wrote this week . "Hockenson's presence gives the team a big-bodied and athletic option to work the middle of the field and red zone. The tight end caught six passes Sunday for 55 yards.

"Interestingly, neither Jefferson nor Hockenson led the Vikings in targets upon facing the Niners," Sobleski continued. "With both on the field and San Francisco's defense concentrating on them, Tai Felton was targeted 12 times and caught a season-high six passes."

With Jordan Addison set to miss his third straight game on Sunday, don't expect Cousins to stray from throwing to Hockenson against the Falcons.

articles.title: Jason Kelce Drops Honest Take After Kansas City Chiefs’ Controversial Loss  to Buffalo Bills
articles.summary: Former Philadelphia Eagles center Jason Kelce took a sarcastic shot at the Kansas City Chiefs’ officiating controversy after their narrow Thanksgiving defeat...
articles.body:
Former Philadelphia Eagles center Jason Kelce took a sarcastic shot at the Kansas City Chiefs' officiating controversy after their narrow Thanksgiving defeat to the Buffalo Bills. Kelce addressed the discussion surrounding a disputed ruling involving Rashee Rice, using the opportunity to revisit complaints about officials allegedly favoring Kansas City.

The Chiefs suffered a 13-10 loss at Highmark Stadium after both teams struggled to generate consistent offensive production in difficult conditions. However, one fourth-quarter decision became a major talking point after officials overturned what initially appeared to be a crucial Rice reception.

Patrick Mahomes connected with Rice on third-and-10 with less than two minutes remaining in regulation. The receiver appeared to secure an 11-yard catch, which would have given Kansas City a first down and an opportunity to continue its potential game-winning possession. Officials initially ruled the play a completion before a review determined that Rice had lost control of the football while going to the ground.

The reversal forced the Chiefs into a fourth-and-long situation near their own end zone, eventually leading to a punt. Kansas City head coach Andy Reid questioned the decision afterward, suggesting the available replay evidence did not clearly justify overturning the original ruling. The call became an immediate source of frustration among the franchise's fans and former NFL players.

Jason Kelce Drops Honest Take After Kansas City Chiefs' Controversial Loss to Buffalo Bills

Kelce shared a blunt take after Kansas City loses to the Bills recently. This can be seen in a post he made on X.

"Well, at least we don't have to hear all of twitter bitch about the refs being homers for the Chiefs tonight," Kelce wrote.

Kelce responded on social media with a sarcastic remark about the recurring accusations that referees favor Kansas City. His message suggested that the controversial decision would make it difficult for critics to continue claiming the Chiefs receive favorable treatment from officials. The former center's reaction quickly became part of the broader discussion surrounding the game.

The Chiefs ultimately failed to overcome the setback, while Buffalo secured the 13-10 victory. Kelce's comments added another dimension to the officiating debate, which has followed Kansas City through several closely contested games. The overturned Rice reception became one of the defining moments of the Thanksgiving matchup, particularly because it removed a promising opportunity for Mahomes and the Chiefs to take control of the closing minutes.

articles.title: J.J. Watt Suggests Steelers Use Mike McCarthy-Inspired Celebrations for Win After Rodgers Remarks
articles.summary: J.J. Watt is hoping the Pittsburgh Steelers celebrated their Black Friday win over the Denver Broncos by embracing Aaron Rodgers' criticism on his way out of the franchise.
articles.body:
J.J. Watt is hoping the Pittsburgh Steelers celebrated their Black Friday win over the Denver Broncos by embracing Aaron Rodgers' criticism on his way out of the franchise.

"If you win this game, you must have 60 ice cream sandwiches waiting in the locker room and break it down on 1, 2, 3 Packers… There's just no other option," Watt wrote in a Friday post on X.

The Steelers ultimately scored two defensive touchdowns in a 27-5 win over the visiting Broncos.

The Steelers announced Tuesday that Mason Rudolph would be starting against the Broncos.

Rodgers responded by going on ESPN's Pat McAfee Show and calling out Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy for not getting to know his defensive players and showing forgetful tendencies like referring to his team as the Packers.

Former NFLer Breiden Fehoko later reported a Steelers player had texted him McCarthy had "a personal assistant who brings him ice cream sandwiches on demand."

McCarthy said after Friday's win he had "not spent enough time with the defense" and planned to look at that aspect of his job in the offseason. For now the Steelers' attention will turn to securing a playoff spot over the six games remaining in the regular season.
